subject: POC scope and success criteria - Acme Corp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC scope and success criteria - Acme Corp

Hi Tom —

Great to meet you and Irene on today’s call. Summarizing the key points and next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of needs:
- Primary: Reduce latency for customer support generative responses to < 300ms median at 95th percentile for single-turn queries (English).
- Secondary: Improve relevance on knowledge-base lookups (match rate target +15% over current baseline).
- Data constraints: No persistent storage of raw transcripts; KV cache only, customer-managed KMS.

Proposed POC (3 weeks):
1) Week 0 (prep): access to a sample of 10k anonymized support transcripts + schema for KB.
2) Week 1: model onboarding + baseline metrics (latency, relevance).
3) Week 2: tuned runtime (batching/quantization) + integration test with a small subset of traffic.
4) Week 3: evaluation & handoff — success criteria review and next steps.

Success criteria (initial):
- Latency: median < 200ms, 95th < 300ms for single-turn responses under test load.
- Relevance: +15% match-rate uplift on the KB test set vs current production.
- Stability: no more than 2% error rate (timeouts/500s) over a 4-hour load window.

Attachments: I’ve attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (ACME_POC_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx) and a shorter success-criteria doc.

Next steps: can you confirm the sample dataset availability and whether Procurement needs a draft SOW before we start prep? If you’re good, we’ll kick off prep on Monday 9/27.

Thanks — talk soon.
—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0147

From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Valdez <irene.valdez@acmecorp.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC scope and success criteria - Acme Corp

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap. Quick clarifications from our side: 

1) We want to add a second use case mid-POC: guided article suggestion where the model returns the top-3 KB articles with brief extraction (title + 1-line summary). That will be a gating factor for our product team.
2) For latency, the product team would prefer 95th < 250ms if possible — can Redwood get there with the tighter requirement?
3) We can provide the 10k anonymized transcripts by Friday 9/24. Procurement has asked for a short SOW to review; they’ll need it before any work that touches production traffic.

If adding the guided-article use case requires more time, we’re open to a 4-week POC but would like a clear re-baseline with updated milestones.

—Tom
Tom Reyes
Director, Product — Search & Assist | Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Irene Valdez <irene.valdez@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC scope and success criteria - Acme Corp

Thanks Tom — that’s helpful context. We can accommodate the guided-article suggestion, but it does change the technical scope. Proposed re-baseline below: 

Updated POC (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): sample dataset + SOW to Procurement (we’ll attach a short SOW and the security checklist).
- Week 1: baseline for both use cases (single-turn responses + guided article retrieval).
- Week 2: runtime tuning for latency/relevance for single-turn responses.
- Week 3: retrieval pipeline + extraction tuning for guided-article summaries.
- Week 4: combined end-to-end evaluation and handoff.

Updated success criteria (v2):
- Single-turn latency: median < 200ms, 95th < 250ms (target).
- Guided-article: top-3 precision >= 70% on our test set; extracted summary accuracy (ROUGE-L) within 10pts of baseline quality threshold.
- Stability: <= 2% error rate during 4-hour windows.

Ownership and asks from Acme: 
- Provide anonymized 10k transcripts + KB export (article id, title, body) by 9/24.
- Identify a technical point-of-contact for quick clarifications (Irene OK?).

We’ll circulate an updated Mutual Action Plan and short SOW by EOD Friday. Lauren and Dev are looped for CS/SE support. If that schedule works, we’ll plan to kick off prep on Monday 9/27.

Action: Tom — please confirm whether Procurement needs the SOW in a specific format and confirm Irene as POC.

Best,
Marissa

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acmecorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Irene Valdez <irene.valdez@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 11:16:00 -0700
Subject: RE: POC scope and success criteria - Acme Corp

Hi team — technical note from our side after a quick review of the KB export you shared: 

- Guided-article retrieval will require an embedding index and a small retrieval service. We can run this within the POC but will need an additional integration window to provision a test index and a thin API to surface results.
- Latency target (95th < 250ms) is achievable for single-turn responses on our Dedicated runtime with batching disabled for front-line requests, but adding retrieval + extraction for guided-article will push end-to-end 95th latency higher unless we: 
  a) run retrieval in parallel and cache top candidates in KV cache, or
  b) accept a slightly longer 95th (we estimate ~300–350ms worst case without caching).

Recommendation: keep the 4-week timeline but add a caching sprint in Week 3 and set a conditional success threshold for guided-article latency: top-3 precision/quality must be met; latency goal for guided-article target 95th < 350ms in the POC, with roadmap items to get to <250ms in production via caching and dedicated indexing.

Attachments: I’ve uploaded a short technical runbook and a proposed integration checklist (SLA_and_Security_Questions.pdf).

If Acme prefers strict 95th < 250ms for both use cases during the POC, we should extend the pilot to 6 weeks to allow full retrieval optimization.

—
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
